quests.title: The Farmer's Treasure

dialogue.t: "It has been over a year since my son, Saimon Jirou, joined the army. He would write letters to us from time to time, and though he has not accomplished much of great note, he would relate everything that happened to him in the army, which comforted this old man's heart greatly."
"The war has continued apace, and my son, who has accomplished little, has stopped sending any letters. This lack of contact has greatly disturbed and wounded this old man's spirit."

"I beseech any who see the notice to help me search for my son. If you know of his whereabouts, whether he ekes out some existence somewhere or has had the fortune of dying for his nation, please let me know, that I may have peace in my heart."
"If you have anything to discuss, I, Saimon Katsumi give you my sincere thanks."
You've returned, youngster!
How have things gone? Do you have any news?
Ah, to think that I've inconvenienced you so on account of my useless son...
Pick some of the fruits and vegetables around my house before you go. I am old, anyway, and there's no way I could finish them.
You mean our village? Well then, you've certainly asked the right man.
Our village gained its fame from producing dyes, and has been the Shogunate's very own dye production facility for as long as anyone records or remembers.
When business was good in the old days, this place was an ocean of red and purple from here to Byakko Plain.

It's a shame that this is not the case anymore... The young people have gone to the city to seek their fortunes, and with the war going on, we have even more trouble keeping people. We cannot keep them, and we cannot hope for their return.
Even my Jirou has... *sigh* I can only hope that he is doing well.
But if you ask me if I regret sending my boy out to the battlefield...
Haha. We people of Konda Village have never regretted such things.
Our ancestors have never feared any foe, not even during the Archon War those millennia ago.
Half our young men went out to battle alongside the divine kitsune in the war five hundred years ago, and they were all slain, never to return... they were also our ancestors.
Every person here is a descendant of samurai — descendants of the victorious dead and the survivors.
No matter how long the peace or lengthy the prosperity, that memory will never fade.
So... If dying for Her Excellency the Ogosho is to be our fate, we have no reason to refuse.
Yes? Do you have any news?
Uh, no, not right now! We're still trying to look for him.
Haha, slow down. Don't rush it, youngster.
*sigh* But at the same time, please don't take too long either.
Finally, someone's here... Please, kind souls, get me out of here! I've been stuck here for several days now...
Sure! C'mon, let's bust this thing open in one go!
Hey! Stop right there, stop!
C—Can you guarantee that this won't hurt me?
Oh come on, we're gonna save you first — everything else can wait!
No! Don't! It's... it's too scary!
And you don't have to be so reckless, I know where the key is!

dialogue.sit: And you didn't think to tell us that first?

dialogue.t: You didn't ask!
*sigh* If you're here to help, you should listen to what people have to say, at least!
The key's in that tree over there. Just help me get it and open this cage.
See that thing glittering over in that tree? That's where the key is.
I'll thank you all properly once I'm out of here.
Hmm, you threw it pretty far, huh?

dialogue.sit: How did you end up in here?

dialogue.t: It's... a long story, and this isn't the place to chat about that. Get me out of here first and then we'll talk.

dialogue.sit: Do you know where Saimon Jirou is?

dialogue.t: I—I do, yes! I'll tell you once I'm out!
I mean, the key's right there! What's stopping you from getting it?

dialogue.sit: Well, stay in that cage a moment, will you?

dialogue.t: Young lad, the world outside your cage has changed greatly since you last saw it...
What...?
We must continue to observe you. We must see if you have the qualities necessary to save this world.
The "trial"... of perseverance!
Wait, Paimon recognizes you! Lord, this is the very person you saw in your dreams!
Ugh, are you both done yet? Help me get that key already!
Is this another "trial"...?
We were just discussing the matter...
Do you outlanders need to hold a meeting just to get a single key?
Ah, but what if you are some sort of great bandit?

dialogue.sit: Perhaps it would be safer if you remained inside that cage.

dialogue.t: That's true... What if he starts growing super huge all of a sudden once we let him out, and he tears us to pieces and eats us, all snicker-snack-like?
Hey! That's not what a bandit does!
Also, what on earth is "snicker-snack"?
Oh no! A werewolf! So scary...
Are you two playing me for a fool here?
What a fierce werewolf!
What are you two, children?
The key is in that tree, so stop playing around already!
Come on, haven't you heard of "mental strength"?
I just know that it has nothing to do with this cage.

dialogue.sit: And that's where you'd be wrong!

dialogue.t: First, you need to create an imaginary space.
Then focus your attention on the cage around you, and imagine it disappearing... and disappearing...
...I've got it.
Talking to you is bad for my mental health.
So, starting from now, I'm just not going to speak to either of you.
Aw, come on, don't be like that!
What a weirdo...
Wow, he's really ignoring us...
Finally, someone's here... Please, kind souls, get me out of here! I've been stuck here for several days now...
Sure! C'mon, let's bust this thing open in one go!
Hey! Stop right there, stop!
C—Can you guarantee that this won't hurt me?
Oh come on, we're gonna save you first — everything else can wait!
No! Don't! It's... it's too scary!
And you don't have to be so reckless, I know where the key is!

dialogue.sit: And you didn't think to tell us that first?

dialogue.t: You didn't ask!
*sigh* If you're here to help, you should listen to what people have to say, at least!
The key's in that tree over there. Just help me get it and open this cage.
See that thing glittering over in that tree? That's where the key is.
I'll thank you all properly once I'm out of here.
Hmm, you threw it pretty far, huh?

dialogue.sit: How did you end up in here?

dialogue.t: It's... a long story, and this isn't the place to chat about that. Get me out of here first and then we'll talk.

dialogue.sit: Do you know where Saimon Jirou is?

dialogue.t: I—I do, yes! I'll tell you once I'm out!
Outlander, what are you doing in the camp? This is a key military location.
...Well, whatever. It's not as if we haven't seen any outlanders recently or anything.
If you're one of them "advisors" from Narukami Island, look for Lord Masahito directly. He'll welcome you, I'm sure.

dialogue.sit: Saimon Katsumi asked us to come here.

dialogue.t: Sorry, I don't know a Sai— wait, you mean Saimon Katsumi?
Old Man Saimon from Konda Village? That's who you're talking about, right?
Ah, so you're a friend of... I see. My apologies, I was rude. Is the old man still well? I hope he's still spry.

dialogue.sit: He's very worried about Jirou, his son.

dialogue.t: Ah. Um, I see.
Well, we're quite worried about him too, to be honest...
Mm... Please don't tell the old man... And definitely don't tell Lord Masahito...
(He left the army...)
I mean, he deserted.
(Quiet, you!)
Yeah, what's so special about deserting anyway?
(You too!)
*sigh* This war is too much to bear.
We've fought quite a few battles against the rebels recently, and we've lost a lot of comrades. They were all our mutual friends...
Of course, Lord Masahito tried to help us settle our emotions a little, and has assigned us garrison duties as a result.
But the Lord Commissioner has been ordering him to send troops out, which must be frustrating him...
Never mind. Back to Jirou, then... That fellow's always liked those stories about great bandits... "Konda Ikki" or something, that was his favorite.
When you add that up with his being tired of fighting this war... I think it's possible that he might have upped and left to join the nearby bandits...
I'm sorry, but that's all I know. If you want to know, you can go ask Ono. He should know more.
See that guy sitting over there, sighing and hanging his head? That's Ono, you can't miss him.
You're too kind. Say hi to Old Man Saimon for me, would you?
Hello there, outlander.
Are you one of those "advisors" sent by the Lord Commissioner to teach us how to fight our wars? If you are, you can just go look for Lord Masahito.

dialogue.sit: Saimon Katsumi asked us to come here.

dialogue.t: Hmph. You outlanders have no manners. Mr. Saimon is well-respected around here. How could you address him without any honorifics?
You're not that polite yourself!
...Alright, I get it. This isn't the time to be arguing about manners.
Since Mr. Saimon trusts you, I should, too.
So, what can I help you with?
Ah, him... he's probably gone off to become a bandit.
Well, for a person of his character, being a bandit is freer than being a soldier.
By the way, don't tell Mr. Saimon this, or he'll get mad.
Jirou actually managed to convinced that scaredy-cat Ishikawa to desert together with him. He made it alright... But Ishikawa ending up eating detention barracks rations for quite a few days!
But even that was because Lord Masahito was kind enough to cover this up and not report it to his accursed old man. If not for that...
*sigh* Let's not even go there... Jirou really got Ishikawa into hot water, I'll tell you what...
If it wasn't for Mr. Saimon, I'd smack him silly the next time we meet!
Well, that's all I know about Jirou. Well, you're going to have to exercise some creativity to make that news a little less unpleasant for Mr. Saimon...
Ah, right. If you'd like to know more, you can go ask Ogura. He's over there by the tower, and was on duty the day it happened. He probably saw more than I did, at any rate.
It was nothing, don't sweat it.
Also, could you not tell Lord Masahito about this?
Jirou was annoying, sure, but this is a matter of life and death. We're not going to go there.
You're... an outlander?
May I ask... what you're doing here in the camp?
If you're not on important business, please leave. This is a key military site. Unrelated persons are not permitted to enter.

dialogue.sit: I'm here at Saimon Katsumi's behest.

dialogue.t: Saimon...? Ah! You mean Saimon Jirou's father!
Sorry for my rudeness, I didn't know that you were here on the old man's request.
I'm not very familiar with Saimon Jirou, but since his family is so worried, I'll do all I can.
That night, I saw him and Ishikawa fleeing northwards. So I followed the usual our private protocol and sounded the alarm after 15 seconds.
Usually, these few seconds would let you find a good spot to hide if you're lucky.
But we never expected that Ishikawa would trip, flip, and fall out of fright... Well, we caught him on the spot.
Aw...
*sigh* That Ishikawa. I mean, you'd think that he would at least act the part of a samurai scion...
If I don't miss my guess, Saimon Jirou has probably fled to Jinren Island, the northernmost section of Narukami Island.
Bandits who refuse to submit to the Shogunate have gathered there, and have increased in number due to the war.
Now that our attention has been shifted to the Sangonomiya and away from them, they're getting all kinds of uppity ideas.
The latest rumors even say that they've tried to set up their own independent nation, or declare a grand revolt against our great Ogosho... or some crazy nonsense like that.
Well, we weren't very well acquainted, but I do hope that Saimon Jirou hasn't thrown in with those fellows.

dialogue.sit: Thanks for sharing what you know.

dialogue.t: I'm just glad that I could help. I mean, everyone has family they miss.
Ah yes. Could you... refrain from reporting this to Lord Masahito?
The issue with the Lord Commissioner is already giving him enough of a headache. He really doesn't need any more trouble.
You're back. Here, have a few Lavender Melon... save them for the road, if you will.
Ah yes, as for young Jirou... Is there news of him?
(Uh, we should probably avoid telling him what's going on...)

dialogue.sit: He's just not at liberty to write to you.

dialogue.t: Ah, is that so... If he is well, it is well.
Thank you. You've done well.
Hehe...
This is good. Ah, my boy truly is a lucky lad. A lucky lad indeed!
Well then! What are you two standing there for? Pack up now, let's go!
L—Let's go...?
Come now! My boy Jirou has experienced so much hardship — I shall go send him some local specialties to pamper him a little!
He must've gone hungry and thirsty many times on the battlefield. Indeed, he must be missing the food back home madly.
And of course, I'll take the opportunity to drop in on Lord Kujou and ask him to "take care" of that useless son of mine, haha!
Y—Yeah... Please calm down, good sir!
Ah, but I am calm. In fact, I am glad! As I shall be, to see my son again...
B—But, your son...

dialogue.sit: The battlefield he's on is super dangerous!

dialogue.t: Right! That's right! It's super dangerous there. Swords flashing as far as the eye can see, arrows falling like rain, and... and...
Cannonballs as big as Paimon falling down and exploding across the land!
They couldn't be that large...

dialogue.sit: We barely made it back here ourselves.

dialogue.t: I see... Well...
Didn't you just say that he's doing well?
He is, yes...

dialogue.sit: Well, we do what we can to survive in war.

dialogue.t: Yup... Yeah, that's right! Jirou's trying so hard on the battlefield. Paimon's sure he wouldn't want you to risk yourself for his sake, right?
It might be impolite to say this, but you wouldn't want to burden your son further when he's in such a tough spot already, right?
You have a point.
Phew...
But I will still go!
What!?
Hmph! The Saimon Clan has ever been loyal! For 2,000 years we have bled for the Ogosho and slain countless evils!
Besides, these old bones have lived long enough. I shall fall in battle in Her Excellency's name. My honor shall not be my own — it shall also be Jirou's!
Just wait here: I'm going to get my heirloom gear, my glittering sword, and then I shall go out with Jirou to meet the foe. There, we shall—
Beat them senseless?
Aye, we shall beat the snot out of them!
Old man! What are you yelling about? I'll bet they can hear you all the way over in Sangonomiya!
You...! How do you know that? Have you even been there!?
And so what if I did? I've had it up to here with you! You know what? forget Sangonomiya, I'm going to Celestia next, and you're not coming along!
Fine! I've lived long enough myself! I'm about to go fight those rebel scum!
Jirou's finally become somebody! Not like you... It's always "this isn't normal, that won't do" with you...

Hah! You? Go out and fight the rebels? You can barely sit down for a game of chess with the young people without talking their ears off about archon-knows-what. You're one to talk about "being somebody"!
And let me remind you, you've never won a single one of those chess games!
(Uh, Paimon thinks we probably step in...)
Oh, so you think you can raise your voice at your old lady? Why don't you just try it, eh?
Look at you! You can't even beat me in an argument! You get to that battlefield with cannonballs that size flying in, and we'll see how you disgrace the Saimon heirlooms and sword!
What do you mean, I can't beat you? I've just never... I've just never been serious!
And if you can't get serious fighting your old lady, do you think you'll do any better against those rebels, huh?
You...!
Hmm?
Just you wait, old woman! Just you wait!
Uh, should we go check on him? It wouldn't be good if he does something rash!
Hah, don't you worry about him!
...He's gone back to his room to flip through a dictionary.
A dictionary...?
He needs it to figure out how to beat me in an argument.
Hmph. Well, he's not talking to me for the rest of week, that's for sure.
But that's better than him going out to the battlefield.
Is that right...
Ah, and speaking of which, youngster from abroad...
You lit that fire under the old coot's rear, didn't you?
Haha! Who were you trying to fool?
And it's about that brat Jirou, isn't it?
Well, let me guess. He's alive... But for some reason, you can't tell the old man what the situation is, right?
Uh... Hehe...
*sigh* Youngster, lying is bad behavior.
...That said, I'm in no position to say that you did the wrong thing.
Hehe, and I must say that it was thanks to your lie that I got to see that old fossil get more fired up than I've ever seen him.
Alright, there's no need to be polite. As it happens, I have a favor of my own to ask regarding that lad Jirou.
Go help me check on that child. Help us see if he's done something wrong or steered himself onto the wrong path.
If he has, help us teach him a little lesson.
Jirou's always been a smart kid, but he's always been a little too pleased with his smarts, and it sometimes blinds him.
I have no fear for him on the battlefield. He's always been good at surviving, no matter where he is.
If he really did meet an unfortunate end... Well, I've long prepared myself for this. That is the nature of war, after all.
I just... fear that he may get too full of himself, bite off more than he can chew, and wind up in a more dangerous position than he expects.
So that's how it is... We'll help you out!
Alright. I won't hold you two here any longer...
While you search for Jirou, I will help to hold the fort here with that old fool. Undo a bit of the damage you did, you know?
Ah, it should be me thanking you. I suspect that our tom-fool son has brought you enough trouble already.
You're too kind.
Phew, finally, someone's here to rescue me!
Thank you, thank you so much!
But we can't stay in this place. Let's split up and get out of here!
Ah, right. I know of a safe spot. Let me just mark it out for you over... here.
Just look for me there, got it? Okay. Great. Bye!
Hey, wait a—
Ugh, he's gone off on his own. So rude!

dialogue.sit: Well, we are a bit too close to the open sea.
The bandits will spot us any moment now.

dialogue.t: That's true. Let's get out of here first, then!
If you hadn't gotten me out of that cage, those fellows would have turned me into a blood urchin...
What's a blood urchin?
Hahaha. Oh right, the two of you are outlanders. You wouldn't know our local parlance.
It's a very scary, ancient method of punishment. A very, very scary one...
Alright, alright, Paimon doesn't wanna hear it! Ugh, why did Paimon even ask!?
No, wait. Actually, how did you know all this weird stuff, huh, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: Hehe. Why don't you try to guess?

dialogue.t: Hey—!
Hahaha, alright, alright. Don't argue.
Ah, so {NICKNAME}'s your name. Pleased to meet your acquaintance.
We want to ask you about a couple of things.
Ask away.

dialogue.sit: So we're looking for a certain Saimon Jirou...

dialogue.t: Oh... him...
Why'd you want to know where he is?
I—It's nothing! I'm just asking.
I... I've heard on the grapevine that the Tenryou Commissioner's sent out lots of ninjas to capture deserters in secret.
Looking at you ask about this and that, I was starting to wonder if the things I heard were true.

dialogue.sit: I know that I'm a ninja?
I said nothing about looking for deserters.

dialogue.t: (This guy's story is just full of holes...)
(Let's just play along and see if we can make those holes any bigger!)
Ugh...!
I— Well, I was just saying that, you know? But yeah, what a coincidence, am I right? Haha... Ha...
A coincidence, you say...
Hehe, did you think that our saving you was a coincidence, then?
There's a fine reward out for providing information on deserters. And if none can be provided, it's no loss as long as we can catch one.
What do you mean "no loss"?
Oh, you've got a good head on your shoulders, don't you? Shame about that...
Wh—What do you mean...

dialogue.sit: (Actually, where'd you learn that line, Paimon?)

dialogue.t: (Hehe! From all the people we've met on this journey, of course!)
Alright, {NICKNAME}. We've wasted enough words on him. Time to execute this deserter.
W—W—Wait!
My life is unimportant but before I die can I please ask to please look at your identification papers please lords can I just know your names please!
What in the world is he talking about?

dialogue.sit: He wants to see our papers.

dialogue.t: Hah! What nonsense.
A man who fled the army, trying to beg for the name of loyal samurai?
Please don't kill me I'll tell you were the treasure is just don't kill me Ogosho's tears please just don't kill meeee!
(This guy's scared out of his wits...)
Calm down. One sentence at a time.
You're... not going to kill me anymore?
Hmph.
But before that, we'd like to ask you another question...
Please ask.
I... maybe...
Hmm?
I—I—I am! I am! I'm Jirou, alright?
Whoa, look at him grovel...
(That's true, his identity is difficult for us to ascertain. But if we send him to his parents, they'll know in a heartbeat.)
Alright, Saimon. On account of your coming from a samurai line, we'll give you one chance to redeem your errors.
Now, tell us again, what... treasure were you talking about earlier? Speak clearly!
Well, I—I'm a professional treasure hunter...
Is he?
S—Sorry! I'll get to the point.
After some lengthy investigation, I've discovered the location of some treasure nearby.
It's just that the treasury gate requires four stone slates to open.
If you could, my lords, please help me find these stone slates, that I might investigate them—
Are you taking us for fools?

dialogue.sit: (Paimon, don't press him too hard, now.)

dialogue.t: I—I wouldn't dare... I just mean that I've investigated it for a while, and have a good deal of experience.
Well, if you do, then you'll know better than to try to play us false.
Once all the stone slates are in place, the treasury door should open. Then we can split the treasure... uh, thirty-seventy...
Hmm!?
You'll get seventy, I'll get thirty!
Relax, relax. This is just business. And we're definitely amenable to price negotiations.
Once we've settled on something that we can agree on, everyone will be happy, right?
True, that seems somewhat unacceptable. How about twenty-eighty?
That's great! Twenty-eighty it is!
Sounds good, {NICKNAME}.
Let's send twenty percent of his fingers to the Tenryou Commissioner. We'll split the remaining eighty.
Eh!? W—Wait, no! Stop! I thought...!
...Halt!
Ah, as I thought, we can still discuss things, right...!
There's no need to dirty your blade. Paimon's will do!
It's smaller, so this'll go slower.
S—Stop! Please stop torturing me!
I'll give you everything. Everything, alright?
Just take all of it... *sobs*
(Wow, we made him cry...)
I'm quite big now... but no one has bullied me like this before... Waaah...
(We played the part a little too well, huh...?)
(Hey! Aren't we done here already!?)
(Okay. Let's go.)
If you hadn't gotten me out of that cage, those fellows would have turned me into a blood urchin...
What's a blood urchin?
Hahaha. Oh right, the two of you are outlanders. You wouldn't know our local parlance.
It's a very scary, ancient method of punishment. A very, very scary one...
Alright, alright, Paimon doesn't wanna hear it! Ugh, why did Paimon even ask!?
No, wait. Actually, how did you know all this weird stuff, huh, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: Hehe. Why don't you try to guess?

dialogue.t: Hey—!
Hahaha, alright.
So you're called {NICKNAME}. My name is Saimon Jirou. Pleased to meet you.
Hmm. That's right, we still don't know how you ended up in that cage.
Well, this is a bit embarrassing... But I was just trying to get some peace of mind from my naggy old father...
Never thought I'd wander right into a nest of bandits and get myself kidnapped!
If not for you, I'd be in mortal danger for sure!
Ah, yes, I forget. I should probably give you some reward for this deed. My apologies.
Hehe, you're too polite...
So, as for the reward...
Yep, yep?
I'm sorry, but I can't give it to you right now.
Come on, then why did you leave us hanging like that?
Whoa, no need to rush. Just slow down a bit and let me talk.
Well, I—I'm a professional treasure hunter.
Professional treasure hunter? Never heard of that...
Uh, I mean, I'm someone who looks for treasure for a living.
Ooh, Paimon's got it now!
After some lengthy investigation, I've discovered the location of some treasure nearby.
It's just that the treasury gate requires four stone slates to open.

dialogue.sit: So you want us to run your errands for you?

dialogue.t: C'mon, don't be so hard up! If you bring the stone slates to me, and let me open the treasury door for you, I won't take a single Mora. The treasure will all be yours.
That's so fishy...
I mean, you did save my life! What's some treasure compared to that?

dialogue.sit: I can't be sure if we can trust you...

dialogue.t: Hehe, ah, see I knew you'd be too kind to take it all.
How about this, then? We'll split it thirty-seventy. Seventy for me, twenty for you, and we'll give that last ten to the Ogosho in taxes. How about that?
Hey! Why do we have to split the loot with the Shogun?
It's a huge treasury, you know? Even twenty percent is a sizable amount!
And it's better than getting nothing, am I right?
Didn't you say that you weren't going to take a single Mora?
Hehe, that was a limited-time offer — you snooze, you lose!
This guy—!
We'll settle this score once we find that treasure, mark Paimon's words!
Oh, you're back? Don't worry about the stone slates. Once you've found them, just give them all to me at once.
Ah, yes, about that... I do have something I'd like you to help me with.
The camp also keeps a little dog. Hehe, we got on pretty well — you could even call us cellmates in a way...
Could you... help me rescue that little fellow?
I remember that the key should be on Red Nose Tsutomu.
He's always drunk out of his gourd... There's no missing him.

dialogue.sit: So, do you know a Saimon Katsumi...

dialogue.t: Uh... Have you met him...?
*sigh* What a headache...
Could you explain that?
I didn't enjoy being in the army. And you've seen how the old man gets when he talks about war...
But you know what? He's lived in peace all this time himself, and he never dared to join the army either... So he just pushed those unfulfilled expectations onto me.
As for me... I was okay with it at first, too. The Tenryou Commission treated us well, and I was making good money!
But then, the real war started up...
Well, the battlefield follows its own logic, of course. But the gain was never worth what we lost.
I couldn't get with that kind of thinking, so I left.
Huh...

dialogue.sit: By which he means that he deserted.

dialogue.t: Oh!
Come on, "deserting" is such a bad word. I prefer something like...
What on earth is that?
What on earth is that?
Right, I remember now. This is what we call "transferring investments!"
Huh...

dialogue.sit: He means going off to become a bandit.

dialogue.t: Ah!
How did you know that I—
Haha, he gave himself up!
Hmph...
Alright, alright. Let's not talk about this stuff... We'll have all the time in the world to talk nonsense once the stone slates have all been found.
Well, you continue then. If you'd like to rest for a while over here, that's fine too.
I'm Saimon Jirou! I'm Saimon Jirou, alright?
The treasure's all yours! I won't take a single Mora!
(Let's not get him too much more worked up than this. He's such a wretched guy...)
Ah, my lords! You've returned.
How is it? How goes your search.
(How are you this experienced...)
Y—Yes, I'm sorry! I spoke out of turn, out of turn!
Please, my lords, rest your weary feet here, and continue on your way once you are rested as you please...
Mm~
Oh, you're back!
So you've been quite idle here, huh?
Haha, there's no need to put it like that.
Sit as you please and have something to eat. This tent of mine isn't too bad, I hope!
Ah, yes. How goes the search for the stone slates?
So quickly? Ah, I should have expected no less from travelers from abroad who move as they please through Inazuma!
No need to rush. At this rate, the day I get rich is not far off, I'd wager!
Uh... *cough*, I mean, "we."
Aye, what say we all get rich together, eh?
Hmph. What a fishy guy...
My lords! Here, sit, please! Sorry for the trouble...
...But how goes your search for those stone slates?
I don't mean to pry!
Ah, so you must have been successful, then?
Hmm?
Please, my lords, continue speaking...
This is all of them, right?
Uh...
Actually... No...
Say that again?
There's one missing.
There's one stone slate missing...
What do you mean "one missing"! We worked really hard to find these four!
And now you say that we're missing one—!
I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I won't do that again!
Hmph!

dialogue.sit: I think we deserve an explanation.

dialogue.t: I've actually hidden the last stone slate somewhere safe. I just wanted to guard against—
Us?
Y—Yes...
Uh, I mean no! Of course not!
I just wanted to prevent people from finding the slates ahead of me...
That way, the one slate that I hid away would serve as a final piece of insurance.
Even if I couldn't obtain the other four slates, no one would be able to open the treasury.
Hmm... Seems reasonable.
So, where did you put that last slate?
I won't!
What?
I don't want to, so I won't!
Wh—What would I be afraid of?
If you made me lead you there and get you the stone slate...
That place is where... people dispose of bodies...
You'd just get rid of me, wouldn't you? Wh—Why wouldn't I be scared...
Whoa, such clear logic!
Well, he's got a point. Why didn't we think of that?

dialogue.sit: Let's do it your way, then.

dialogue.t: Hey! I haven't told you where the stone slate is hidden yet!
Are you just going to get rid of me... right here? The secret of the stone slate will die with me, you know?
J—Just spare my life, and I'll tell you where it is. And after that... I'll do whatever you tell me.
(Let's not press him too hard. And since he's already said this much...)

dialogue.sit: Tell me where to find the slate.

dialogue.t: There's a place, beside a small waterfall, hidden amongst the cliffs across the sea from Ritou. That's where I buried the stone slate.
If you fear you might forget, my lords, I'll mark the location on your map later...
Thanks!
Hmph. Looks like you've got your uses, huh?
How are things going? I can already smell the treasure, haha!
Mm-hmm, us too!
One, two, three, four... Hmm, no, that's not right.
Eh—?
We're missing one slate.
This guy is untrustworthy. He's trying to play us!
D—Don't be so hasty! Let me explain.
I hid one other stone slate beforehand — here, beside a waterfall amidst the cliffs on Ritou's opposing shore. Here, I'll mark it out on your map.
I just need you two to go on one last trip.
Really...? Paimon still thinks this is suspicious.
There won't be, don't worry.
See, if I didn't have that last slate, I wouldn't be able to get to the treasure either, would I?

dialogue.sit: Then why didn't you tell us from the start?

dialogue.t: Well, I didn't trust you all as much then. But since you've both helped me so much, there's no reason for me to hide anymore.
...You do have a point.
I'll leave it to you two, then. I'll be resting here. Just look for me again once you've found it.
Hmph. Aren't you a pair of idle hands.
We're doing all the work here... Maybe we should renegotiate our terms!
Wait! We had an agreement on that one! You'll have a majority share!
Are you sure?

dialogue.sit: He's panicked, that's what's for sure.

dialogue.t: Well, since you look like you want that treasure so desperately, we'll trust you just this once.
We're definitely gonna renegotiate once we get our hands on that last stone slate.
Please go, you two. Time waits for no one!
Who are you? Name yourselves!

dialogue.sit: That's our line. Who are you?

dialogue.t: What's that got to do with you?

dialogue.sit: I will not cut down a nameless person.

dialogue.t: Hah! You outlanders have such a rule as well?
How interesting...
There's no need to waste time here, just fight him already!
Uh, okay...
You've come to save this kid?
No, she(he) hasn't...
Silence, you!
A—Alright, you speak first.
We're here to settle a score with him!
Oh? What a coincidence!
I'm here to do just that myself!
In which case, I'm afraid you're going to have to get in line.

dialogue.sit: Hmm. Would you like to know...

dialogue.t: ...Who saved him the previous time?
You did.
He told me so at least a few times.
He bluffed you into helping him find the stone slate, didn't he? Bet he didn't tell you that the treasure still needs a key to open it, huh?
A key?
Hah! You see, the treasury doesn't just have one gate, but three.
Want to open that door? Slates, key, you'll need 'em both.
This fellow is a little snake. Had us all fooled.
How about this? I suggest that you and I settle this whole treasure business between us.
From the looks of you, you aren't with the Shogunate. That suits me just fine. I'd sooner trust an outlander than one of those lackeys.
And if you can prove your ability, I'll let you into my group. It's a good deal for you!
Oh, him? I'll have the dogs tear him to shreds. We'll pack the pieces up and chuck 'em into the sea.
You have other dogs?
What do you mean by that?
I mean that Toratarou doesn't bite.
And how do you know that?
He's a good dog, he wouldn't bite anyone!
I think you're in need of a few dog bites, alright!
But that's the thing. Toratarou wouldn't bite anyone! He's a real friendly dog!
Shut up!
But...
But, but, but! Just shut up already, or do you need me to smash you, cage and everything!?
Now, where were we?

dialogue.sit: You were talking about a key...

dialogue.t: It's on his person.
That smart aleck thought that he could hide the treasury key and keep all the treasure for himself.
But he was way too hasty for his own good. He's just full of openings!
Now in our line of work, the most important thing is a sense of "fairness."
Things don't end well for those who try to hoard everything for themselves.
It's just the principle of the matter, you know? And when someone doesn't listen to his brothers, then slightly... harder measures are required.
So he fled into the cage, locked himself inside, and threw the key away—
What...?
I know, right? He stunned us right into silence too.
And then he gave a cry of shock—
I threw the wrong key... I threw the cage key into the trees opposite us.
Pfft!
Bwahahahahaha! What in the world is that?
So, the person you're trying to save is this hapless, worthless man.
Not much to his character either: he's a deserter, hated by all!
And finally, he even got on the bad side of someone he couldn't afford to offend!
But you on the other hand — you're a smart person. You've got brains, brawn, and you've got your ways.
Between him and I, it should be pretty obvious who you should choose, eh?

dialogue.sit: I wouldn't call myself that intelligent.
I'd say you're the unintelligent one here.

dialogue.t: ...And what do you mean by that?

dialogue.sit: The treasure. I'm taking all of it.
I'll take both him and the treasure.

dialogue.t: Alright!
Is that so... Well, that's a shame. A real shame.
N—No! D—Don't come any closer!
Noooo! I wanna go home! I don't wanna be a bandit! Or a treasure hunter!
There, there... We're here to rescue. We're gonna take you home.
No! No! I want to live! I still want to see my mother...!
Agh, now Paimon's feeling guilty...

dialogue.sit: You know what, I'm actually quite glad.

dialogue.t: (Just look at him! Paimon doesn't think he's gonna listen to a word you say... We might as well just keep up the act!)
Stop! Stop! Don't come any closer!
I—It's like this, alright?
You've caused us lots of trouble, and your repeated deceptions are a sin that cannot be atoned for!
You have contributed to the Shogun's righteous cause in aiding in the defeat of these bandits!
By these actions have you thus redeemed yourself, and thus, you shall not be punished. Indeed, we shall bring you home to be reunited with your parents!
Hey, Jirou, are you alright?
Hello! Jirou! Are you there?
Is this...
Is this... some kind of newfangled interrogation technique?
Pfft! No, it isn't! We're going to bring you home! C'mon, aren't you happy?
Oh...
Ohh...
Ohhhh!
Whoa, what are you trying to do, bite someone?
...So you're saying that not only am I not going to be "dealt with," but that I made a contribution, right?
Hahaha! That's right, that's right! That was my intention all along!
I won't beleaguer you with the details, but I was merely baiting those crooks in when I was captured the previous two times...
I redirected you and intentionally got myself captured, for I had calculated perfectly that you would find me here, just as I fell into the trap!
But little did they know that I had risked myself to serve as the lure while you closed the net! Ah, like the praying mantis hunting the cicada, they did not see th—

dialogue.sit: We were just randomly passing by.

dialogue.t: *sigh* Indeed, even the wisest of the wise cannot account for every coincidence.
Of course, I'm not calling myself wise here. I am a very humble person, after all.
Whoa, and here we were worried that we might have scared the stupid out of him...
Seems like this guy has forgotten everything.

dialogue.sit: I'd say that his thick skin is a small miracle in and of itself.

dialogue.t: Hehe. Well, now that you've said all this, I feel like there's no need to go home just yet!
*sigh* This guy is... Ugh, he's such a waste of our breath!
Why don't we just get all that treasure while we're at it. Two big scores in one day shall set us all at ease.
Hmph. *If* there's any treasure, you mean...
But why don't we go have a look anyway? We've come all this way. It'd be a shame not to take some of that treasure~
That's more like it! Here's the key. Don't lose it, now.
Phew... I... I'm very sorry, you two.
To tell you the truth, I—I'm still a little frightened by everything that happened...
Oh, forget that for now. We're here for the treasure, y'know? The treasure!
*sigh* Don't... be in such a rush. Just let me take a break, and we'll head off.
Hmph. You can forget about fooling us this time, Jirou!
I won't. I wouldn't dare...
*sigh* You know what? I'll just give you the key. Just don't lose it now.
And don't worry, it isn't the cage key this time...
What in the world is all this...
*cough* Pah...! So much ash!
We've looked all over the place. Nothing but rotten provisions and old pottery...
Famous swords and armor, precious gems and gold... There's nothing like that here.
There's nothing hidden underneath, either...
Why did this happen?
Hey! You aren't tricking us again, are you!?

dialogue.sit: He isn't tricking us this time.

dialogue.t: Huh...? But there's nothing here!

dialogue.sit: I think I get what happened...
I'll explain it to you later, Paimon.

dialogue.t: What is this!? We did so much, planned for so long, but in the end...
Uh, come on, don't get too down...
Alright, come on, there's no need to be so sad. Let's go home, shall we?
Maybe you think that returning home empty-handed might be embarrassing, but actually, it's fine...
You've been through three super dangerous adventures, and you survived.
The mistakes you've made have also been made up for. Though you didn't get the treasure you expected, you didn't lose anything in the end anyway...
Compared to all those dangers you've been through, being scolded by your dad is nothing, right?
Alright...
Let's go home, Jirou.
(Yay! We did it!)
Ho there, youngster! I do not recognize your face. Did you see the notice as well?
Yes, haha. Does it appear like anyone else nearby is young?
Oh dear, where are my manners?
Well met, youngster.
I believe you must have seen that notice earlier. As you may suspect, I am Saimon Katsumi.
It brings me no small amount of shame to ask outsiders to help me find that useless son of mine...
But please, do tell me if you hear of anything regarding him, alright?
No matter if that little brat is alive, or... *sigh*
Please tell me everything you know truthfully.
You have my thanks. Truly...
It's fine, leave it to us!
Ah yes, youngster. Let me also say that if you're able to enter and exit military camps... you could simply ask that lad's comrades-in-arms.
There's another young lad who joined the army together with him. Ishikawa, I think his name was. A military family's son, and a reliable one at that.
I'm sorry to have kept you here for so long. Still, if you receive any new, don't forget to swing by Konda Village and inform me.
Alright, I need to go back to the village now. Stay safe, youngster.
Ho there, youngster! I do not recognize your face. Did you see the notice as well?
Yes, haha. Does it appear like anyone else nearby is young?
Oh dear, where are my manners?
Well met, youngster.

(Hey, this has got to be Jirou's "long-winded old man," right?)
*cough* Is something the matter?
Eh? N—Nothing! Everything's fine!
Well then, allow me to continue from where we last left off...
It brings me no small amount of shame to ask outsiders to help me find that useless son of mine...

Alright, I need to go back to the village now. Stay safe, youngster.
Haha! My Jirou's back!
You little brat! Bet you've been slacking off instead of fighting for Her Excellency like you ought to have, eh? And to top it off, you didn't even have time to write to me!
Working hard at everything but fighting, am I right?
Wait. What do you mean?
It means you're an old mouth breather...
This kid can always count on your falling for his fibs. But not me — I always see through his little lies.
I'll bet he ran away to have his own little adventures because he thought army life was hard, boring, and dangerous.
...Just like you when you were young.
Lazy, impatient, and feckless, but fond of a good brag. Ah, you men are all the same...
Hey! Why'd you start trashing me all of a sudden?
Let him speak for himself! What happened?
Well... It's a long story...
Hahahahaha! You're... You're an embarrassment!
Hahahahahaha! The what to the what now? What is this nonsense? Hahaha!
I'm ashamed to call you my son!
Just go and be a comedian in the city — and don't come back, you hear?
Hehe, I'm just glad that you didn't lose a limb, Jirou.
Though to be honest, we'd be more relieved if you did...
Whoa. That's a guy's real parents for you, huh...?
So... are you two really ninjas from the Tenryou Commission?
If you ask me...
Nope!
...Pfft!
Ahahahahahahaha!
Hahahaha... All right, give our son a break, you old geezer.
But you've been laughing at me too, mom!
Well, again, we're just glad that you came back safe.
After all, you only had to join the army because of that little crime you committed...
Ever since you left, neither we nor the village chief have been able to protect you.
But you've got to learn to look out for yourself, too. How to choose your path wisely, how to assess the risks...
You're a clever kid, but that's not enough when you're away from home. You need to be cautious and...
All right, that's enough nagging, you old fossil. What our boy needs right now is a bath and a good rest.
Um, Paimon heard you mention that he committed a "little crime."

dialogue.sit: So, about his being a deserter...

dialogue.t: Oh, it was nothing... Just a stupid mistake made by some reckless young men who bit off more than they could chew.
I wouldn't call it a mistake though...
Ahem!
Y—Yes, as I was saying, they made a mistake, and there was no excuse for that.
Ah! Silly me! I've talked so much but left your payment out!
Well, since my own son isn't worth pinning my hopes on... I'll hand our heirloom blade over to you!
Please accept this priceless family heirloom of ours as weregild for his life.
I hope that the path ahead won't render this blade bloodstained, youngster...
Hah! I wouldn't worry about that — this blade's so blunt, it's nearly turned back into a billet!
Tch, old woman! Don't show such disrespect to our heirloom blade!
Come, take this drawing with you as well.
See? This is how our blade used to look like...
Look at that beautiful pattern...
The smooth arc...
The lovely cross section and sharp edge...
Alright, alright. How long are you going to caress that artwork, huh? Give them the gift already!
Hmph...!
Take good care of them, youngster.
Oh, right! Take our heirloom armor too! I was gonna give it to Ichirou, but he's also good for nothing... so it's yours!
Geez, stop it! Can't you see how this armor's practically dripping rust!? You're embarrassing yourself!

dialogue.sit: But your gifts are more than enough already...

dialogue.t: Alright, alright then...
Thank you once again, youngster from a foreign land...
I wish you good fortune in your adventure ahead.

quests.description: Saimon Jirou, a son of a farming family, dreams of finding treasure, but has met with an unexpected crisis instead…
